Orkas Brings Local-First Multi-Agent AI Teams to the Desktop

03 Nov 2026, 06:30 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: github.com

2 min read

Overview of Orkas

Orkas is an open-source (MIT licensed) and local-first multi-agent desktop application designed to handle complex workflows by breaking goals down into actionable steps. Rather than acting as a single conversational chatbot, the platform utilizes a central "Commander" to coordinate tasks, delegate work, and manage projects directly on a user's machine.

Core Features and Architecture

The software ships with 16 built-in specialist agents covering various domains, including video production, research, content writing, design, and office tasks. Additionally, it integrates with popular command-line interface (CLI) tools and external agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Hermes-Agent.

  • Local-First Design: Conversations, files, and custom knowledge bases remain stored locally on the user's disk by default.
  • Task Automation: Features include to-do lists, auto-advance capabilities to progress through items sequentially, and scheduled automations running hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.
  • Library and Document Search: Users can index local PDF and document files, allowing the app to search passages and generate answers complete with source citations.
  • Flexibility in Model Selection: The application supports the built-in Orkas model, external API keys (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, and others), or local endpoints compatible with OpenAI.

Practical Implications and Verification

Orkas is tailored for users seeking a continuous, multi-agent workflow rather than a single-prompt assistant. The application offers packaged installers for macOS and Windows, while Linux users can run the tool from source (requiring Node 22.12+ and glibc 2.34+).

Because specifications, pricing plans, and feature sets can change, readers should verify the original announcement, licensing terms, and system requirements directly via the official GitHub repository or official documentation before deployment.
